key_insight: Decoupling exploration from optimization lets RLVR search for novel reasoning strategies without harming the final student model.
engineering_relevance: For math-reasoning LMs, this provides a safer training recipe to improve diversity and performance while avoiding the quality regressions caused by putting novelty pressure directly on the optimized policy.
method: Train explorer policy/policies with an added novelty bonus
Filter sampled trajectories for correctness and quality
Distill accepted trajectories into a separate student policy without novelty bonus, then repeat across rounds
evidence_signal: The abstract reports results on seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model families, with ExpDis outperforming DAPO at the same wall-clock budget and improving pass@k scaling.
watch_item: Filtering and distillation quality are critical: if novelty samples are noisy or the verifier is narrow, exploration gains may not transfer cleanly to the student.
paper_title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
